questions.question: According to the speaker, what happens to the Z‑Z curve?
questions.explanation: The speaker explicitly says, “Well, that moves the Z‑Z curve up.”

evidence.quote: Well, that moves the Z-Z curve up.

original_segments.text: Well, that moves the Z-Z curve up.
Output will go up, and then there will be a multiplier.
So output will go up by more than the initial increasing
goal and expenditure.
That's what we had before.
It will go up by more, but not as much
as it did in the closed economy.
So the increasing output will be more than the increasing
government expenditure, but it will be not as much as it would
have been had we had a close economy.
Why is that?
Why is the last part true?
Why not as much as it would have been in the close
economy?
Well, you can read it here.
It's because part of that extra energy, the amount for
consumption, will go to foreign goods.
So it will not come back to demand
more domestic production.
And that's reflected in that the trade deficit,
in this particular example, we start with a situation
where the trade was balanced.
